clues.text: This city sits on the south bank of a big river in the South, close to the center of its state. Flat delta land gives way to low hills just west of here.
clues.narrowing: Points to a river city in the South, near the middle of its state.

source.quote: The city lies on the south bank of the Arkansas River close to the state's geographic center in central Arkansas.

clues.text: Summers here are hot and sticky, and winters are cool with hardly any snow. Yet the heat has hit 114, and the cold has sunk to 12 below zero.
clues.narrowing: Rules out mild towns; keeps a southern city with sticky heat, cool winters, and wild swings.

source.quote: with hot, humid summers and cool winters with usually little snow

clues.text: The seat of rule moved to this river town in 1821, from a post that kept flooding. It has stayed here ever since that move.
clues.narrowing: Cuts the list to a capital moved in 1821 from a flood prone post.

source.quote: The legislature moved the capital to Little Rock, where it has remained ever since.

clues.text: A French explorer in 1722 named this place for a low stone ledge on the river bank. Boat crews used that ledge as a landmark as they passed.
clues.narrowing: Nearly decisive: one capital took its name from a low stone ledge by a river.

source.quote: Little Rock was named for a stone outcropping on the bank of the Arkansas River used by early travelers as a landmark

clues.text: The governor of Arkansas works in this city. State lawmakers meet here, at the seat of state rule.
clues.narrowing: Confirms it: the governor and state lawmakers of Arkansas work in this city.

source.quote: Little Rock is the capital and most populous city of the U.S. state of Arkansas.

reveal.blurb: This city was founded in 1821 as the territory capital, on a river bank marked by a famous stone ledge. In 1957, nine brave Black students walked into Central High here and changed the nation. Little Rock is the capital of Arkansas.
